 4 MVC No.4836/2019  JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Santhosh S., who is husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioners No.2 and 3, son of petitioners No.4 and 5 and brother of petitioners No.6 and 7, in a road traffic accident.

As per the direction of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru, in MFA No.2636/2023 (MV-D), judgment dated 10-09-2024, the matter is taken up again for fresh consideration, in the light of the observations made in the said judgment and for determination of quantum of compensation and liability.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 16-05-2019, at about 10.50 p.m., the deceased Santhosh S., was proceeding on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-14-V-9290, on NH-206 bypass road,
Vishveshwaraiah cross, Bhadravathi, Shimoga District
, by observing traffic rules and regulations and by observing the vehicles movement, he was carefully crossing the road.

At that time, the Ambulance 108 came from Tarikere side, without siren and indicator movements, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life,
without observing traffic rules and regulations, came from right side and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
Due to the said impact, the deceased fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to MAX Hospital, Shimoga, wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter he was shifted to KMC Hospital, Manipal, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
During the course of treatment he succumbed to the injuries on 20-05-2019 at about Sushmitha .R vs District Health Officer on 10 July, 2025

3 5.15 p.m.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working in Vijay Techno Crats Private Limited and earning a sum of Rs.17,895/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Bhadravathi Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said 108 Ambulance Tempo Traveler for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C.

The respondent No.1 is the owner, the respondent No.2 is the authorized vehicle release owner, the respondent No.3 is the driver and respondent No.6 is the insurer of the 108 Ambulance Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-51-G-5176.
Likewise, the respondent No.4 is the RC owner and respondent No.5 is the insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-14-V-9290.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.2, 5 and 6 have appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.2 and 5 have filed their written statement.
The respondent No.6 did not choose to file its written statement.
Whereas, the respondents No.1, 3 and 4 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondents No.1, 3 and 4 are placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.2 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has admitted that, he is the RC owner of Ambulance vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-G-5176, the said vehicle was driven by one Srinivas D.T. and he was having valid driving licence vide DL No.KA14-19992002138 at the time of accident.

Further he has contended that, the ambulance vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-G-5176 was under insurance coverage with the Karnataka Government Insurance Company, vide insurance policy bearing No.1234283 and the same is valid from 22-04- 2019 to 21-04-2020.
Hence, he is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, the respondent No.5 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has contended that, the accident took place due to rash and negligent act of the deceased and alleged accident is a self accident and the jurisdictional police have investigated the matter and filed the charge-sheet against the deceased.
The deceased has stepped into the shoes of the owner/fourth respondent, who is the father of the deceased.
Hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy bearing No.2404023118P115067735 in favour of respondent No.4 in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-14-V-9290 and it was valid as on the date of accident.

Further it is contended that, the motorcycle had been driven by a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same at the time of accident and the owner of the said vehicle has knowingly allowed the person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same and there is a violation of the terms and conditions of the policy by the respondent No.4.
Hence, it is not liable to indemnify the insured, as per the terms and conditions of the policy.

It has contended that, the deceased drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner, without observing the traffic rules and regulations and crossing the road without observing the vehicle movements on the road and dashed Sushmitha .R vs District Health Officer on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168293972/
4 against the vehicle bearing No.KA-51-G-5176, which was coming opposite side and caused accident.

The deceased was the main architect of the alleged accident and the alleged accident is a self accident and police have filed charge-sheet against the deceased and the driver of the ambulance bearing Reg. No.KA-51-G-5176.
It has denied the age, income, avocation, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by the deceased.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.4, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Santhosh S., has succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident, alleged to have been occurred on 16-05-2019, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the 108 Ambulance Tempo Traveller bearing registration No.KA-51-G-5176 ?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?

Further, they have got examined two more witness namely Mahantesh and Ravikumar as P.W.2 and P.W.3 respectively and closed their side.
On the other hand, the respondents No.2, 5 and 6 have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.

11. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of their oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 26.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is notarized copy of driving licence, Ex.P.5 are notarized copy of Aadhar cards (total 6), Ex.P.6 is notarized copy of ration card,

Ex.P.24 is attendance card from January-2019 to April-2019, Ex.P.25 is request letter to Axis Bank and Ex.P.26 is Axis Bank pass book.
12. Further, the petitioners have examined one more witness by name Ravikumar S/o Kenchegowda as P.W.3, who is said to be the eye-witness to the accident in question.
The P.W.3 has deposed in consonance with the evidence of P.W.1.

He has clearly deposed that, on 16-05-2019, at about 10.50 p.m., when the deceased Santosh S., was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-14-V-9290, on NH-206 by-pass road, Vishweshwaraiah Cross, Bhadravathi, Shimoga District,
was carefully crossing the road, by observing traffic rules and regulations and by observing the vehicles movement, at that time, the offending Ambulance 108 came from Tarikere side, without siren and indicator movements, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing traffic rules and regulations, came from right side and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
Due to the said impact, the deceased fell down and sustained fatal injuries.
Further he has deposed that, at the time of said accident and he noted down the registration number of offending Ambulance i.e. KA-51-G-5176.

Further he has deposed that, immediately after the accident the injured Santosh was shifted to Max Hospital, at Shivamoga and he has recorded his statement before the Bhadravathi Traffic Police Station and he has shown the place of accident to the Police.

Further he has deposed that, the accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Ambulance bearing Reg. No. KA-51-G-5176.
13.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 3 and 12 to 20,
prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 14-V-9290 by the deceased and due to rash and negligent Sushmitha .R vs District Health Officer on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168293972/
6 driving of the driver of offending 108 Ambulance Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-51-G-5176.

Further it reveals that, due to said impact, deceased Santhosh S., has sustained grievous injuries on his face, abdomen and all over the body and succumbed to said injuries during the course of treatment at KMC Hospital, Manipal, on 20-05-2019 at about 5.15 p.m. The investigation officer in his final report/charge- sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.3, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-14-V-9290 and the driver of offending 108 Ambulance vehicle bearing No.KA-51-G-5176 and the deceased Santhosh S., has sustained grievous injuries on his face, abdomen and all over the body and succumbed to said injuries during the course of treatment.

14. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of 108 Ambulance Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-51-G-5176 and motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-14-V-9290 in the said accident, the ownership of respondent No.1 over the 108 Ambulance Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-51-G-5176, ownership of respondent No.4 over the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-14-V-9290 and the respondent No.5 & 6 being the insurers of said vehicles respectively, as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioners has remained undisputed by the owner, driver and insurer of offending 108 Ambulance Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA- 51-G-5176/Respondent No.1, 3 & 6, as they did not choose to contest the case of the petitioners.

Even, the respondent No.5 insurance company has not denied the accident in question and involvement of 108 Ambulance Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-51-G-5176 and motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-14-V-9290 in the said accident.

It is taken specific contentions that, the accident has occurred due rash and negligent act of the deceased, as the deceased drove his motorcycle in rash and negligent manner, without observing the traffic rules and regulations and was crossing the road without observing the vehicle movements on the road and dashed against the Ambulance bearing Reg. No. KA-51-G- 5176, which was coming from opposite side.

Further it is contended that, the deceased was the main architect of the alleged accident and as such the Police have filed charge- sheet against the deceased and the driver of the ambulance bearing Reg. No.KA-51-G-5176.
But, the respondent No.5 has failed to establish the said contentions.

The respondent No.5 has neither adduced any evidence to establish the contentions taken in its written statement, nor it has produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners.
Even, the respondent No.5 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the accident in question has taken place due to due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-14-V-9290 by the deceased and due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending 108 Ambulance Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-51-G-5176.

Further it reveals that, due to said impact, deceased Santhosh S., has sustained grievous injuries on his face, abdomen and all over the body and he was succumbed to said injuries during the course of treatment at KMC Hospital,
Manipal, on 20-05-2019 at about 5.15 p.m.

It is strange to note that, at one instance, the respondent No.5 in its written statement has specifically contended that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased motorcycle rider and he is the main architect of the said accident and at the other instance, the learned counsel for respondent No.5 has made suggestions that, the deceased rider of the motorcycle is not responsible for the accident and the said accident has solely occurred due to negligence of the driver of ambulance.

One cannot be Sushmitha .R vs District Health Officer on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168293972/
7 permitted to blow hot and cold at the same instance.

sentences.text: Further, as per the document produced and relied by the petitioners in support of their oral evidence i.e. Ex.P.3 charge-sheet, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-14-V-9290 and the driver of offending 108 Ambulance vehicle bearing No.KA-51-G-5176.
Admittedly, the said charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the owners of offending vehicles or the petitioners.
In such circumstances, the petitioners cannot seek the Court to rely one part of the said document and ignore the other part of the said document.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited V/s Premlata Shukla, reported in (2007) 13 SCC 476, has clearly held that, "If a party produced a document and once the same is proved, he cannot seek to rely one part of the document and ignore the other parts of the document.

15. Further, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence affidavit that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Ambulance bearing Reg. No. KA-51-G-5176 and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased rider and he has recorded his statement before the Police with respect to same.

But, neither P.W.3 nor the petitioners have produced the copy of his statement recorded before the Court, to show that, he has stated the same facts and circumstances of the accident in his statement also, stating that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Ambulance bearing Reg. No.
KA-51-G-5176 and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased rider.
Non production of statement of P.W.3 in the case, leads this Court to draw adverse inference on the veracity of evidence of P.W.3.

In absence of corroborative documentary evidence in support of oral evidence of P.W.3, it would be unjust to rely solely on the oral evidence of P.W.3 and hold that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Ambulance bearing Reg. No.
KA-51-G-5176 and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased rider.

On the other hand, all the police documents produced and relied by the petitioners in the case clearly speaks about the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-14-V-9290 in the cause of accident.

16. Further, the Ex.P.15 spot mahazar and Ex.P.16 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on NH-206 Bypass road, Vishveshwaraiah Cross, Bhadravathi, Shimoga District, in between 108 Ambulance bearing No.KA- 51-G-5176 and motorcycle bearing No.KA-14-V-9290,
while the said motorcycle was crossing the road.
Further it is pertinent to note, as per Ex.P.12
Motor Vehicle Accident report
, the accident has not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both the offending vehicles.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents to disprove the case of the petitioners and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to sole negligence of the driver of 108 Ambulance bearing No.KA-51-G-5176 and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased motorcycle rider.

sentences.text: Further, the Ex.P.18 Post-mortem report clearly speaks that, the deceased Santhosh S., has died due to haemorrhage secondary to blunt force traums to the head, face and abdomen, sustained in the road traffic accident.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.3 final report/charge- sheet has clearly stated that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of 108 Ambulance bearing No.KA-51-G-5176 and deceased rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-14-V-9290.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the driver or the owner of offending vehicles.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending 108 Ambulance bearing No.KA- 51-G-5176 and motorcycle bearing No.KA-14-V-9290 in the said accident, rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both the offending vehicles and injuries caused to deceased Santosh S., in the said accident and the cause of his death.

18. Further, the evidence on record clearly establishes that, there is equal contributory negligence on the part of the driver of offending 108 Ambulance bearing No.KA-51-G- 5176 and the deceased rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA- 14-V-9290 in the cause of accident.

If the driver of offending 108 Ambulance bearing No.KA-51-G-5176 had taken care and if he had not driven his vehicle in rash and negligent manner, he could have stopped or slow down his vehicle immediately by applying the break and avoided the accident.

On the other hand, if the deceased/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-14-V-9290 had not ridden his motorcycle in rash and negligent manner, if he had been diligent and taken care while crossing the road, which is National Highway, the accident would not have occurred.
There was equal responsibility of taking required care and caution on both the drivers while passing through the junction of roads.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the driver of 108 Ambulance bearing No.KA-51-G-5176 and the deceased/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-14-V-9290 have equally contributed in the cause of accident.

Accordingly, holding that, the drivers of both the vehicles are equally responsible for the damage caused in the said accident,
would be justifiable and will meet the ends of justice.

19. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased Santhosh S., has succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident, occurred on 16-05-2019 at about 10:50 p.m., on Sushmitha .R vs District Health Officer on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168293972/
9 NH-206 Bypass road, Vishveshwaraiah cross, Bhadravathi, Shimoga District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of 108 Ambulance Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-51-G-5176.

But,
they have failed to prove that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of 108 Ambulance bearing No.KA-51-G-5176.

As discussed above, the oral and documentary evidence available on record clearly establishes that, at the relevant point of time of accident even the deceased/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-14-V-9290 was riding his motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and he has also equally contributed in the cause of accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that, the accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending 108 Ambulance bearing No.KA-51-G-5176 and the deceased/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-14-V- 9290 and the deceased Santosh has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident and succumbed to said injuries during the course of treatment.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In this regard, they have produced their respective Aadhar cards and ration card, which are marked as Ex.P.5 & 6.

The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children,
petitioners No.4 and 5 are the parents and petitioners No.6 and 7 are the sisters of deceased Santhosh.

On the other hand, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased Santhosh is not specifically denied by the respondents in the case and even there is no rebuttal evidence with respect to same has been produced by the respondents.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Santhosh S.
23.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

28. Liability:

Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.6 is the insurer of the offending 108 Ambulance bearing No.KA-51- G-5176 and likewise, the respondent No.4 is the owner and respondent No.5 is the insurer of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-14-V-9290.
